experiments.title: Length can grow while energy falls
experiments.question: Can an exact certificate explain the transient that a norm plot hides?
experiments.scope: Exact rational example and CAS identities; no new kernel-checked theorem, rounding or plant model.
experiments.next_test: Check rational certificates for a family of sampled closed-loop matrices with interval perturbations.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject a candidate if P or P minus A-transpose P A loses positive definiteness.
experiments.conclusion: The first step increases squared length from 1 to 449/400 while energy drops by exactly 1.

experiments.title: Delay consumes a calculable distance
experiments.question: How much clearance does a smaller delay buy under fixed bounds?
experiments.scope: A sharp 1D constant-acceleration model. Equality allows boundary contact. Rejection is not a stopping action.
experiments.next_test: Replay measured timestamp-to-actuation traces with independently justified acceleration and braking bounds.
experiments.kill_criterion: Stop if any trace exceeds an assumed delay or braking bound; do not narrow bounds to improve admission rates.
experiments.conclusion: The bounded rule has no false admissions in 972 constructed cases; the nominal rule has 294.

experiments.title: The gain balances two errors
experiments.question: Can completion of squares expose the optimal gain and its assumptions?
experiments.scope: Scalar error variance with positive variances and zero cross-covariance; no stochastic calibration or multivariate claim.
experiments.next_test: Estimate cross-covariance on held-out sensor traces before using the independent-error gain.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject the independent-error model if residual correlation invalidates its objective.
experiments.conclusion: Every tested gain has exactly the predicted nonnegative excess variance; a correlated fixture changes the optimum.

experiments.title: Saturation breaks an innocent rewrite
experiments.question: May a command-combining pipeline regroup saturated additions?
experiments.scope: Exhaustive finite integer tables for four clipping bounds; not a classification of real-valued controllers or a new algebraic theorem.
experiments.next_test: Check actual command-combining operators and compiler rewrites against frozen finite countermodels.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject any reassociation rule when one input triple changes the applied command.
experiments.conclusion: Clipping is idempotent on the tested inputs, but saturated addition is not associative.

experiments.title: A reachable interval can hide holes
experiments.question: When does a compact reachable-set description erase useful structure?
experiments.scope: All 127 nonempty subsets of seven integers, three independent additive steps. No PFR theorem transfer or general compression benefit.
experiments.next_test: Compare exact unions and interval hulls on quantized actuator models with measured checking cost.
experiments.kill_criterion: Abandon compression if it excludes any reachable state or its membership cost exceeds the exact representation.
experiments.conclusion: With increments {-3, 3}, three steps reach four points; the integer interval hull contains nineteen.

experiments.title: Low entropy does not remove a rare failure
experiments.question: Can uncertainty or average error replace a hard support bound?
experiments.scope: Constructed two-point distributions. Probabilities and moments are exact; displayed logarithms use floating point. This is our falsifier, not a result attributed to Tao.
experiments.next_test: Compare mean, quantile and support contracts on the same held-out perception errors.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject any hard-safety implication based only on decreasing entropy or mean-square error.
experiments.conclusion: Entropy and mean-square error decrease while the worst possible error stays at 10.

experiments.title: Feasible does not mean optimal
experiments.question: Can a checker keep feasibility separate from objective quality?
experiments.scope: Exact arithmetic on the upstream displayed witness and 17 common translations. No execution replay of the elimination algorithm; grid optimality is finite only.
experiments.next_test: Require separate feasibility and bound certificates from one real allocation consumer.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject an optimality claim when a feasible point with smaller cost is supplied, even if the solver terminated.
experiments.conclusion: Both displayed points are feasible, but their costs are 1 and 0. The strict gap survives every tested common translation.

experiments.title: A lower bound is not a schedule
experiments.question: When do workload and critical-path bounds miss the optimum?
experiments.scope: All 1,024 forward-edge DAGs on five labeled unit jobs, plus one eight-job fixture, on three identical machines. Offline, no release times, WCET, transport, or RTOS model.
experiments.next_test: Add release times and bounded transport costs, then compare independently checked schedules against the exact small-instance oracle.
experiments.kill_criterion: Reject a quality claim unless feasibility is checked and its attained makespan matches a sound bound.
experiments.evidence: Exhaustive finite search + separate feasibility checker
experiments.conclusion: The elementary bound is loose on 2 of 1,024 five-job DAGs. The layered eight-job fixture has lower bound 3 and optimum 4.

witness.stronger_bound: Four jobs in each of two nonoverlapping layers require at least two slots per layer.
